data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Neurotoxin from Clostridium botulinum (onabotulinum-, abobotulinum-, incobotulinumtoxin A)

## Mechanism of action
- Heavy chain binds cholinergic nerve terminals; light chain (zinc protease) cleaves SNAP-25 → acetylcholine cannot be released
- Result: temporary chemodenervation of muscles (3–4 months) and eccrine sweat glands (6–9 months or longer)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Hyperhidrosis: axillary (approved), palmar, plantar, craniofacial, compensatory
- Aesthetic: glabellar lines, crow's feet, forehead lines, platysmal bands, masseter hypertrophy, gummy smile
- Others: Hailey–Hailey and Darier disease (reduces sweating-triggered flares), rosacea flushing, keloids (adjunct), Raynaud phenomenon, Frey syndrome, anal fissure
- Microbotox/mesotherapy (intradermal dilute injections) for skin texture and sebum

## Dose & formulations
- Axillary hyperhidrosis: 50 U onabotulinumtoxin A per axilla intradermally (after starch–iodine test)
- Glabellar lines: 20 U (5 sites × 4 U)
- Reconstitute with preservative-free (or preserved for less pain) saline; units are not interchangeable between brands (abobotulinum ~2.5–3 × onabotulinum units)

## Adverse effects
- Injection pain, bruising, headache
- Spread to adjacent muscles: ptosis (eyelid — use apraclonidine drops), brow ptosis, asymmetric smile, hand weakness (palmar injections)
- Antibody formation (non-response) with frequent high doses
- Distant spread (rare): dysphagia, breathing difficulty — boxed warning

## Contraindications
- Neuromuscular disorders (myasthenia gravis, Lambert–Eaton, ALS), infection at site, pregnancy and breastfeeding, allergy to albumin

## Drug interactions
- Aminoglycosides, quinine, calcium-channel blockers, other neuromuscular blockers potentiate effect

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid (insufficient data).

## Viva points
- Cleaves SNAP-25 → blocks acetylcholine release
- Sweat effect lasts longer than muscle effect
- Brand units are not interchangeable
- Ptosis — treat with apraclonidine eye drops

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.60 (Botulinum toxin injections); Khopkar ch.35 (Botulinum toxin; mesotherapy). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
